title: THE ORACLE OF KING LEMUEL
mv: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, It is not for kings to drink wine, Nor for princes intoxicating drink.
mvp: “It is not for kings, O Lemuel, It is not for kings to drink wine, Nor for princes intoxicating drink.” Proverbs 31:4 (NKJV)
assignment: Identify five (5) “strong wines” that can destroy destiny (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: King Lemuel is a biblical character mentioned twice in the book of Proverbs 31. Lemuel received his mother’s word of wisdom on the proper ways kings must conduct themselves by purity, piety, justice, clarity, fair play, etc. Our focus is the word of advice to royals to stay away from strong drink (alcohol), just as he was taught by his mother.

A beverage or drink is a consumable liquid to quench thirst and prevent dehydration. These beverages can be categorised into alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages. An alcoholic or intoxicating beverage is any drink containing alcohol.

The consumption of these intoxicating beverages causes unwarranted excitement and loss of comportment (Proverbs 20:1). Drinking alcoholic beverages is a leeway to drunkenness because being intoxicated is a result of the alcohol content acting as a central nervous system depressant and decreasing brain activity and sensory functions (Isaiah 5:11).

Taking alcoholic drinks often leads to some negative outcomes which affect the quality of life physically, socially and mentally (Genesis 9:21-22). The most common include hangovers, impulsive behaviours (Esther 1:10-12), impaired judgements (Isaiah 5:22-23; 28:7), financial difficulties (Proverbs 21:17), relationship struggles (Genesis 19:32-36), avoidable accidents, injuries, etc. (Proverbs 23:31-35). Evidently, alcoholic intake also has some long-term negative health effects like heart problems, cancer and liver disease (Proverbs 23:29-32).

A person is tagged as royal when the individual is a king, queen or a member of the royal family. They are often classified as people of royal blood and status; as a result, they are not people who are expected to misbehave. According to Revelation 1:6, anyone washed in the blood of Jesus and genuinely born again is a King and priest unto God.
King Lemuel, as well as ‘Royals’ are advised that:

i: The royal blood must stay away from alcoholic drinks so as not to forget the law and pervert justice for the afflicted (Proverbs 31:5).
It is only those who want to perish that are encouraged to take strong drinks (Proverbs 31:6).
It is only foolish people who are lured to take strong drinks because alcohol is a mocker (Proverbs 20:1).
God specifically instructed Aaron and his children to stay off strong drink (Leviticus 10:8-9). This instruction still applies to us because we are priests (Revelation 1:6).

Anyone who wants to experience true joy or feel elated, should get filled with the Holy Ghost (Galatians 5:22; Ephesians 5:18). Psalm 4:7 says, ‘‘You have put gladness in my heart, more than in the season that their grain and wine increased.’’

b.x: Strong drink is deceptive, and whosoever is deceived by it is not wise. Get filled with the Holy Ghost to be truly elated!

i: What are the negative outcomes of taking non-alcoholic drinks?
Briefly explain your position of royalty as a believer.
